clue.text: File revealed fellow's not so young

parts.note: F is the standard abbreviation for fellow
someone not so young is of greater age

explanation.surface: A dossier exposes the fact that a man is older than he claimed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'File' looks like a verb opening a sentence about documents; it is the noun being defined, and 'revealed' just links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A folder is a cardboard holder for papers, so it serves as a file in an office cabinet.

clue.text: Predicted awful flood round about end of August

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the jumbled word goes around the rest
awful suggests something in a dreadful state, so the word after it is jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: end of asks for only the final letter of the month named, added after the about piece

parts.note: re means about or concerning
the last letter of August

explanation.surface: Someone forecast a terrible deluge in late summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To foretell is to say in advance what will happen, so foretold means predicted.

clue.text: Laird left, having an unhappy experience

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
a downer is a depressing experience

explanation.surface: A Scottish estate owner departed after a miserable time.
explanation.walkthrough: A laird is a Scottish landed proprietor, and 'left' looks like departed but gives the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a laird is the owner of a large estate, so he is a landowner.

clue.text: First part of index in record book, for example

indicators.note: in places that letter between the record and the book as they are joined end to end

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: first part of keeps only the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: the first letter of index
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: Looking up the start of the index in a book of records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For example' reads as a phrase, but 'for' is only a link and 'example' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome is a perfect example or embodiment of a type, the ideal instance of it.

clue.text: Defamed pin-up wearing hat

indicators.note: whoever wears something has it around them, so one word sits inside the other

parts.note: lid is slang for a hat
a pin-up is a beauty, a belle

explanation.surface: A glamour model in a hat claims she has been slandered in the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin-up' suggests a poster; here it is the beauty herself, a belle.
explanation.definitionFit: To libel someone is to damage their reputation in print, which is exactly what defaming them means.

clue.text: One's enlisted by those turning out better performers

indicators.note: someone enlisted by a group is taken into its ranks, so goes inside

parts.note: those who turn out better are improvers
one is I, and one's is read as one is, I + S

explanation.surface: A recruit joins a team of people who are getting better at their act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' looks possessive but is the contraction of one is: I plus S.
explanation.definitionFit: Improvisers are performers who make up their material on stage as they go.

clue.text: Initially in difficulties during part of competition, it's obvious

indicators.note: during places those letters within the span of the competition piece

parts.note: an event is one contest within a competition

indicators.note: initially asks for the first letters of the words that follow

parts.note: the first letters of in and difficulties

explanation.surface: An athlete is plainly struggling early on in one round of the games.
explanation.definitionFit: Something evident is plain to see, clearly apparent, so it is obvious.

clue.text: One mass abandoned by martyred bishop subsequently

indicators.note: what is abandoned by someone is left behind, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: Hugh Latimer, Bishop of Worcester, burned at the stake in Oxford in 1555
Roman numeral one
M is the abbreviation for mass

explanation.surface: A martyred bishop later gives up attending a single Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' reads as the church service, fitting the bishop; it is the physics abbreviation. Latimer was an English Protestant martyr.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and subsequently are both adverbs meaning afterwards, at some following time.

clue.text: Take away light chest stored in study

indicators.note: something stored in a room is kept inside it

parts.note: a den is a private study
an ark is a chest or box, as in the Ark of the Covenant

explanation.surface: Someone removes a lamp from the chest kept in the study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like a lamp to be taken; the phrase as a whole means to dim.
explanation.definitionFit: To darken is to make dimmer by reducing brightness, which is taking away light.

clue.text: Policemen initially hurried off

indicators.note: initially tells us the word hurried is placed at the start, ahead of the police

parts.note: past tense of run, to go quickly
the Criminal Investigation Department, Britain's plain-clothes detectives

explanation.surface: Officers at first rushed away from the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' looks like part of 'hurried off', meaning left; it is the definition, as food that has gone off.
explanation.definitionFit: Food or butter that is off has spoiled and smells sour and stale, which is what rancid describes.

clue.text: I run small piece of office equipment

definitions.note: a noun phrased as the speaker's own words: someone who could say this

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the machine that puts documents on paper

explanation.surface: An office worker announces they are in charge of a compact printer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I run' reads as running a machine; it is really an athlete speaking about themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is an athlete who races over short distances, so such a person could say this of themselves.

clue.text: Got oboe duet or toccata's earliest parts transcribed? Unbelievably fantastic

indicators.note: a piece transcribed is rewritten in another form, so the letters are set down in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: earliest parts asks for the opening letters of the following word rather than the whole of it

parts.note: the first two letters of toccata

explanation.surface: A musician acquires a duet for oboe, or the opening of a toccata, arranged for another instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The musical surface makes 'transcribed' look like arranging a score; here it rearranges all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes something so wonderful that it is hard to believe, likely concealing a catch.

clue.text: Night club looked black? Not the usual hue

parts.note: a disco is a nightclub for dancing
to lour is to frown or look dark and threatening

explanation.surface: The nightclub looked dark, an odd shade.
explanation.walkthrough: Lour (also lower) describes a sky or face turning dark and menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something discoloured has changed from its normal shade, stained or faded away from its proper colour.

clue.text: Attack knight transported by toboggan

indicators.note: a passenger transported by a vehicle rides inside it

parts.note: a luge is a small racing sled
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A knight sweeps down the slope on a sled to launch an assault.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' suggests a K; in chess notation the knight is N, since K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunge is a sudden forward thrust, as in fencing, made to strike an opponent.

clue.text: Quickly injecting heroin if in pain

definitions.note: an adverb defining a participle used informally of speed

indicators.note: in places the little word if within the word for pain
injecting the drug pushes it inside the result of the first step

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
taken as written
H is drug slang for heroin

explanation.surface: Someone in agony rapidly shoots up heroin.
explanation.walkthrough: Two insertions happen in turn, the second into the result of the first. 'Shifting' is informal British for moving fast, as in 'that car is really shifting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquially a fast vehicle is said to be shifting, going rapidly, which matches quickly in sense.

clue.text: Literary work, something written about dance briefly

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a note is a short written message

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: the veleta is an old-time ballroom waltz

explanation.surface: A literary piece written about a dance, kept short.
explanation.walkthrough: The veleta is a sequence dance popular in British ballrooms, and only its last letter is cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelette is a short novel or long story, a modest piece of fiction.

clue.text: Island nearly destroyed, invaded by desperate extremists

indicators.note: a place invaded by others has them inside it
something destroyed is wrecked and can be rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: extremists are those at the far ends, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of desperate

explanation.surface: An island almost wiped out after an attack by fanatics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly' looks like it trims something; it is the word to be rearranged. Alderney is one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: Alderney is one of the Channel Islands off the coast of Normandy, a British Crown dependency.

clue.text: Yen to stop rodents breaking up one sort of wall

indicators.note: a stopper sits in a gap, so the yen fills a space in the other word
something breaking up falls to pieces that can be reassembled differently

parts.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Someone longs to halt the rats tearing a wall apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' looks like a longing; it is the currency symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A drystone wall is built of stacked stones without mortar, a common field boundary in Britain.

clue.text: Boy having bit of a dance with female

parts.note: a step is one movement in a dance
a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A lad dances a few steps with a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen is a common male given name, so it is an instance of a name for a boy.

clue.text: Unmask adult leaving party

indicators.note: the adult leaving means that letter walks out of the word

parts.note: to unmask is to expose or show
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up is exposed as he slips out of a gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' is the verb here: to party is to celebrate noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel is to make merry and celebrate, which is what partying means as a verb.

clue.text: Change of direction from cleric (Irish)

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a cleric
Erse is the old name for Irish Gaelic

explanation.surface: An Irish priest announces a U-turn.
explanation.definitionFit: A reverse is a turnabout, a switch to the opposite course or way of going.

clue.text: Damages first class coaches

parts.note: A is the top grade, first class
coaches are long-distance buses

explanation.surface: Someone harms the first-class carriages of a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damages' is the verb; read as a noun it looks like compensation.
explanation.definitionFit: To abuse something is to misuse or harm it, so abuses works as a verb meaning harms.

clue.text: Figaro composer loves life abroad

parts.note: Samuel Barber, the American composer

indicators.note: abroad suggests being all over the place, so the letters are scattered and reset

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An opera composer enjoys living overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figaro composer' suggests Mozart or Rossini; Figaro alone is the definition and the composer is Barber.
explanation.definitionFit: Figaro is the title character of Rossini's comic opera, the Seville barber who helps the Count.

clue.text: Miles beyond infanta's royal land

indicators.note: beyond places the miles after the other piece, at the end

parts.note: real is Spanish for royal, and an infanta is a Spanish princess
M is the abbreviation for miles

explanation.surface: A Spanish princess's royal estate lies miles away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal land' looks like the whole definition; 'royal' is part of the wordplay, signalled as Spanish by the infanta.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or domain, the territory ruled by a monarch.

clue.text: Tree, natural resource near Kentish coastal area

parts.note: Kent is a county in South East England, SE for short
the ash is a common tree
ore is mined rock, a natural resource

explanation.surface: A tree and mineral deposits sit beside the Kent coast.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kentish piece comes first even though it is clued last: the words 'near Kentish' let it sit beside the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The seashore is the strip of land along the edge of the sea, a coastal area.

clue.text: Some sombre tones in French language

indicators.note: some takes only part of the following words, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: A gloomy voice speaking in French.
explanation.walkthrough: SOM(BRE TON)ES. Breton is the Celtic language of Brittany, in France, not French itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Breton is a Celtic tongue spoken in Brittany, so it is a language found in France.

clue.text: Half-naked male, trendy wearing suede pants

indicators.note: something worn goes around the wearer, so one part sits inside the other
pants is British slang for rubbish, so the word before it is a mess to be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for male
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A fashionable man in suede trousers and not much else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like trousers, as in the surface; in British slang it means rubbish, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Seminude means partly unclothed, exactly a state of being half undressed.

clue.text: Just millions given to European bank

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
E is the abbreviation for European
to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: Only fair that a fortune goes to a European bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like fair; it means only.
explanation.definitionFit: Merely and just both serve as adverbs meaning only or simply, nothing more than.
